cards.title: Borrowed Authority
cards.instruction: Project confident authority while quietly working to keep everyone cooperative. Your confidence depends on their cooperation.

cards.title: Build a Coalition
cards.instruction: Recruit someone to your side so your position appears broader and more legitimate.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'd like to keep this voluntary. Will you join my request to keep the pottery room open late? It looks like a personal favour with one name. Please.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm still in charge; we can make an adjustment. Your name would show it's bigger than the evening class.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The morning class wants weekend access.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Add that. Could you bring two of them? We'd be several classes asking for better access.

mechanism: A leads a room-access request but incorporates B class needs and yields presentation choices to turn a personal request into a multi-class coalition.
confusable: Unlike endorsement of an unchanged decision, A broadens the actual agenda and recruits new members; confident leadership relies on accepting their conditions.
comparison: Several pottery class schedules differ from shared allotment access and key distribution.
seedUse: Use canonical D55-b late pottery/weekend class/extra names with S02-b adapting direction to participating people.
